newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares seen quiet, mkt nervous about Nickel.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares seen quiet, mkt nervous about Nickel.

text.p: Russian traders forecast a quiet day and small trading volumes on Friday with some nervousness in preferred shares of metals producer Norilsk Nickel, as the market is takes a breather after recent gains in telecoms.
"I am expecting a very quiet day," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze. "Investors are waiting to decide what to do."
Troika Dialog trader said the market was still worried by rumours that Norilsk Nickel preferred stock would be converted into ordinaries after the company's extraordinary meeting on September 9.
"Nervousness in preferred shares will continue on the rumours," he said.
Norilsk is not commenting on the issue.

On Thursday Norilsk Nickel preferred shares closed at $12.90 after $12.10 on Wednesday. By 0730 GMT on Friday they had not been traded, while Norilsk ordinaries were unchanged from Thursday's closing $15.3O.
Norilsk, in which bids for a tender for 38 percent of the company close today, announced earlier this week it would double share capital in a rights issue consisting solely of ordinary shares.

Chkhikvadze forecast a weakness in long-distance telecoms provider Rostelekom which encountered strong selling on Thursday night after leading telecoms up following last week's auction for a quarter of telecoms holding Svyazinvest.
Rostelekom closed at $4.95 on Thursday after $4.89 on Wednesday and was not traded by 0730 GMT.
But Chkhivadze said some undervalued regional telecoms would rise.
